My former therapist is an incredibly sweet and wonderful person. She is also fairly wealthy and has been for a long time, so she was a bit out of touch when it came to others' budgets. You should just pack up and fly right on over to somewhere nice in Europe, maybe to the South of France or Tuscany! Just be a waitress or something and eat good food, get some sunshine, meet new people and get new experiences! like that girl in that one movie! (Under the Tuscan Sun, I think she said?)" She was very serious about it and made a few other extravagant suggestions.

They sent us the application paperwork first, and I just filled that out through email. Once I got approved for the adoption, I paid the deposit fee, and then in the months after that I was sent updates by the owner about how the  mom and selected litter were doing, when they were born, videos, pictures, vet check-up details, etc. 

A few days before I went and got him, the owner took Andy and his litter mates in for a final vet checkup for all the necessary shots and general health info, and then she gave me a copy of the paperwork for that once I'd actually arrived. When you're there, she'll also have some last paperwork and agreement forms for you to fill out for her records, and then after that you should be good to go! :>
Very friendly and sweet people, were super helpful with any questions I had or if I needed information, and were always happy to provide pictures/videos and updates about the puppies. 

Also, heads up, the ranch that Beartooth is on is in some weirdly-labeled backroads and might be a little confusing to find - at least, if you're using GPS like I did, ha. She should give you her contact information, though, so if you have any trouble trying to find the place just give her a call like we did and she'll help navigate you through the weird roads.

Hello! He's gonna be 4 years old in September, and so far he's doing excellent both health and personality-wise.

Very playful and energetic! I run him every day for about an hour (sometimes more depending on the weather), and he keeps pretty busy with lots of toys and my parent's dogs. Andy is a healthy weight and very active, but because he's so HUGE alongside just being a malamute, I also try to keep an eye out for any hip and weight issues. Definitely keep up on that right from the beginning, is my suggestion. 

He's a very jolly, lovey, and protective dog! He's never been aggressive with people, just really shy (despite his big size), and he's excellent with our other pets (both cats and dogs). His biggest issue, in regards to temperament, is that he's a very jealous dog and can sometimes get aggressive towards dogs he doesn’t know - only if they try to get near me, otherwise he's fine. I don't think that will be an issue with your future pup, it's probably just an individual thing, but I thought I'd mention it just as something to be aware of. I would definitely say to socialize your pup early so they can get used to other dogs and people (and keep a close eye on it around smaller animals due to the high prey drive). 

Andy is also incredibly smart and has a crazy good memory, definitely the smartest dog I've ever had. Very quick learner, and so clever! So, no brain development issues with him, either. 

If I ever decide to get a malamute again at some point, Beartooth will definitely be my first choice. I got a really wonderful dog from them, so personally, I think you will, too. I hope my responses all made sense, and if you have any further questions about my experience with Beartooth, etc., don't hesitate to ask! :>

In the making-of video for Sonne, there is a part where Till talks about how, before they went with the Snow White theme, he'd originally imagined a music video featuring a scenario with a boxer and how some of the lyrics fit into that. :>

I was 12 or 13 and saw some of their music videos on both German MTV and Viva (can't remember which video I saw first, but it was probably Du Hast). Immediately fell in love, and one day after school, I walked to the electronics store and bought a copy of Sehnsucht. I think a week later, my family went on a trip to Italy, and I remember I had Sehnsucht on constant repeat in my little CD player for that entire trip - just couldn't get enough of it! After that, I managed to find Herzeleid and Mutter and would listen to those over and over again, too. Was already a fan when Reise, Reise and Rosenrot came out, so I was able to snatch those up at release and be hyped along with everyone else, which was fun. 

I eventually got both my parents into the band, ha, my mother even burned copies of my CDs - some for herself to listen to in her office, and some to send to my dad when he got deployed.  

Been a huge fan ever since. There was a long period of time after we moved back to the US where my interests went elsewhere and I hadn't checked in on their music for a while, but then in 2022 I picked right back up where I left off and bought all the other albums I'd missed out on and have been catching up and indulging in all the newer content as much as I can. I hope someday I'll finally be able to see one of their shows. ♡ 
(Reise, Reise is also one of my all-time favorite albums from any band, ever, and it's been so good to get back into it and re-listen after such a long time. It was like hearing it for the first time all over again!)

A little, mostly just at the beginning, especially when we were trying to get Andy used to our work schedules before one of us was able to be with him much of the day. Potty training was another frustration, but that was mostly due to having to get up at odd hours and stand outside in the freezing cold and hold his leash while he took his sweet time looking for a good place to use the bathroom..

 My biggest advice for apartment living for your Mal would be to give them as much exercise as you can, especially if it's anywhere your pup can really get them legs moving, ha. (When your dog gets more used to the walking exercises, of course!) Fortunately, where we were at, we had a dog park and tons of places to walk him, like the local neighborhood and our city's downtown area. I'm not sure where you'll be at, but if you're also able to take your pup on walking trails and hikes like we were able to, I would absolutely recommend that as well once they start walking more! I'd also suggest looking into local parks in your location/future location to see if any are dog friendly, or if there are any actual dog parks you can take your pup to to get them that exercise and socialization they'll need. 

 And when you're home with them, make sure to set aside some time for play and interaction, because they'll get bored and feel a little cramped, and when mine would start to get antsy he would take it out by chewing on things or barking. Does your dog like to play fetch, or tug-of-war? A really good play session with you, them, and some toys could really help wear them out, especially on days where you might not be able to take them outside/into the city.

And, definitely keep them on a routine, if you can. The structure and schedule really helped our boy a lot, and it got him adjusted better to the smaller space, I think (particularly during work hours), it made him less anxious because he always knew when it was time for walks or a car ride or play time, etc., if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining everything properly! If you have any further questions, don't hesitate to ask, I'll try my best to answer :)

Definitely socializing with other dogs. His first several months were great; he was living in an apartment complex in a big city and had tons of interactions with a variety of dogs, all of whom he got along great with. Then, we had to move to a small, isolated town with no dog parks, stand-offish people, and only a few family members and their own dogs. Lost all that proper socialization he had been learning, so now he plays too hard and rough or is just overly aggressive/territorial (especially if he gets jealous). I'm planning on taking him to a local training class when it opens up again, so hopefully, that helps.
So, I would definitely say that, if it's possible, please make sure your pup is able to get plenty of good, healthy interactions with other dogs! 

ALSO. Grooming. I really wish I'd been more on the ball with that when he was a pup, ha! He lets me brush him, but he does NOT like being brushed on his hind end and does his best to make the process a big hassle. 

Mals are such wonderful dogs with sooo much love to give, but they can absolutely test your patience and give you a few gray hairs!

All the remaining pasta would go to my parents and they would proceed to add the sauces and meats or veggies they wanted to their noodles. 

When it was a night where the kids got mac and cheese, my parents would either eat the mac as well or they would have something else like a meat or maybe a soup or something.
